Chinese chipmaker CXMT shares surge on Shanghai debut

Chinese chipmaker CXMT's shares surged nearly 470% on its Shanghai Stock Exchange debut, reaching a market value of 3.28 trillion yuan. The surge occurred despite US sanctions, which some coverage suggests could incentivize the company to strengthen domestic chip production. The initial public offering was described as Asia's biggest IPO. Analysts from Nomura suggested the stock could rally over 1,200% based on market share gains.
